questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code uses the connection pool? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
Two runners call leaseJob at the same moment while three jobs are queued. What does FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED cause?
choices: Each runner locks and claims a different queued job instead of blocking on the same row
Both runners claim the same oldest job and one UPDATE fails
The second runner waits until the first commits, then claims the same job
The second runner always gets null because a row is locked

questions.prompt: With connectionTimeoutMillis: 0, what happens to pool.connect() when all 8 connections are in use?
choices: It waits indefinitely until a connection is released
It opens a temporary connection beyond max
It retries every 15 seconds because of statement_timeout

questions.prompt: completeJob is called for a job that was never leased (state is still 'queued'). What happens?
choices: The job is marked succeeded or failed anyway
An error is thrown because no row matched
The job is moved back to running
The UPDATE matches no rows and the job is left queued, with no error
